new_findings.title: Clustering job authorization bypasses the dedicated pool
new_findings.defect: The operator entitlement repository defaults to get_optional_session, which creates a session from the business async_session_factory. The clustering jobs route injects get_clustering_session but passes no session-bound entitlement repository to the authorization gate, so the gate uses the business pool before its clustering-pool transaction.
new_findings.failure_scenario: If the business pool is saturated while the dedicated clustering pool remains available, get_optional_session can yield None after its connection probe fails; authorize_operator_control then returns 503 and paid clustering jobs cannot use the available clustering pool.
new_findings.fix: Use a cluster-specific, separately scoped entitlement session on the dedicated pool, or move the entitlement read into the route-owned clustering transaction; add a route test where the business session is unavailable while the clustering session is available.

summary: All five recorded claim findings still hold as fixed with targeted unit assertions. The lane suite stopped at the aiosqlite fixture timeout and PostgreSQL integration tests were not run per brief; a medium clustering-pool isolation gap remains in the new operator entitlement dependency.
